//: The Celery worker: a second Railway service, built from this same repository and this same Dockerfile, started differently.

It has to be the same image as the web service. A task is queued by name, and the worker resolves that name in its own code -- a worker running an older build either does not know the task or runs the old version of it, and neither failure says so out loud.
To create it: Railway > New > GitHub Repo > this repository, then in the service's Settings set Root Directory to `backend` and Config-as-code path to `railway.worker.json`.

Variables it needs, all shared with the web service: DATABASE_URL, DJANGO_SECRET_KEY, CELERY_BROKER_URL, REDIS_URL, the EMAIL_* set, DJANGO_FRONTEND_URL, and the AWS_* set if object storage is on. A worker with a different DJANGO_SECRET_KEY renders invoices nobody can download; a worker with no EMAIL_* silently drops every notification it was given.
DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS is not needed -- nothing makes an HTTP request of this process.

Do not set CELERY_BROKER_URL on the web service until this service exists and is consuming. With a broker set and no worker, every .delay() is accepted, queued, and never runs: invoices stay unrendered and the mail never arrives, with no error anywhere.

Overrides the image's CMD, which is entrypoint.sh -- migrate, then gunicorn. The worker must do neither. Migrations belong to exactly one process, and two processes racing to apply the same migration at deploy time is how a half-migrated database happens.

--concurrency 2 rather than the default, which is one process per CPU. The work here is rendering PDFs and waiting on SMTP, and each child holds its own database connection; on a small plan the default opens more Postgres connections than the tier allows and the worker dies on connect.
--max-tasks-per-child recycles a worker process periodically. ReportLab holds onto memory across renders, and a long-lived child on a 512 MB container is eventually killed by the OOM reaper mid-task.
deploy.//restartPolicy: A worker that exits has lost its broker connection or been OOM-killed. Both are recovered by starting again; neither is recovered by staying down.
deploy.//healthcheck: Deliberately absent. A worker binds no port, and a health check against one that does not exist fails the deploy every time.
